title: indigo_agent_scheduler: precess targets to the date of the sky grid so plans do not depend on the wall clock, refresh the stale visibility_kept_only_with_starts fixture
description: Found while working on ticket ffac50e4 (2026-11-25). indigo_test/build/unit/test_agent_scheduler_plan fails case visibility_kept_only_with_starts with 'unit/test_agent_scheduler_plan.c:1393: assertion failed: info.compact_value > info.value'. Reproduced with the master version of the scheduler sources (header parser rebuilt into the archive); the test builds its headers directly, so it is independent of the @twilight default change. Probably related to the latest VISIBILITY change 704bc478e (keep a VISIBILITY plan as it is while nothing changes, re-plan when a run ends 10 s off its planned end), which may have changed the moment the 39th random queue's COMPACT plan overtakes the kept plan; to confirm. Decide whether the code or the test's expectation (the chosen queue/time t = now + 3009) is wrong, and fix it. This failure makes the configured 'unit' flow check fail for every ticket.

outcome.summary: Reviewed diff master...HEAD (sky.c 2 lines, DRIVER_VERSION, SCHEDULER.md line, plan test fixture, new sky test). Rebuilt in scratch (no worktree changes): worktree unit binaries sky+plan pass. Code: target_build() and reachability() now precess @target with indigo_j2k_to_eq(indigo_eq_of_date(UT2JD(sky->start))), consistent with Sun/Moon per grid point; no other wall-clock input in sky/plan/night/header (plan.c uses indigo_monotonic_time only for info->seconds; budget is a work count). sky->start is the right epoch for both functions; live agent rebuilds the grid hourly at now, so the epoch moves by <= ~1 h (~0.01 arcsec), negligible, and target grids built between rebuilds are now consistent with the sky grid. Verified with an LD_PRELOAD time() shim: new code gives identical plan values at wall clocks 2023, 2026, 2060; old code drifts. New sky test target_in_coordinates_of_grid_date fails on master sky.c (unit/test_agent_scheduler_sky.c:123, 41.9998 vs 42.1840) and passes with the fix; 0.33 deg dec shift for 60 yr at RA 0 is correct; 2840140800 = 2060-01-01 00:00 UTC. Re-derived fixture: loop 0..66 = 67th queue; at now+13182 compact 220.50 < value 267.03 (fails), at 13183/13184 compact 269.74 > 267.03, so the comment (kept against a higher COMPACT at the moment it overtakes; replaced as order alone) still holds. SCHEDULER.md line accurate; formatting ok; git diff --check clean. FINDING (record accuracy, not code): the causal diagnosis in the 09:20 note is not supported. With master plan code the ORIGINAL fixture (39th queue, now+3009) fails at every wall-clock time I tried (scan 1.70e9..1.90e9 step 2e6 s and 1795300000..1795600000 step 600 s, plus 2000 and 2060), with compact_value ~352.6 vs value ~433.8, a gap of ~81 while the wall-clock effect is ~1e-3/day; with the epoch fix it still fails. The new fixture passes with the old sky code too. So the failure is a fixture stale against the plan code (the earlier passing check is unexplained, possibly a stale build; cl

history.text: Cause: targets precessed to wall-clock epoch; switching to the sky grid epoch

Reproduction: test_agent_scheduler_plan visibility_kept_only_with_starts fails on master (also with the plan code of 704bc478e^), deterministically and when run alone, although the identical tree 0bb29906 passed the unit check at 2026-11-25 01:43 UTC. Cause: indigo_scheduler_target_build() and the reachability check precessed @target with indigo_j2k_to_jnow(), i.e. to the wall-clock epoch, so a plan for fixed inputs drifted with the time the tests ran and the knife-edge fixture (39th random queue, t = now + 3009) crossed its threshold. Fix: precess to the epoch of sky->start (indigo_j2k_to_eq(indigo_eq_of_date(UT2JD(sky->start)))), as the Sun and Moon already are. The fixture is re-derived by a scan under the fixed epoch: the first queue/time where the kept plan is kept against a better COMPACT plan and replaced as an order alone is the 67th queue at now + 13183 s (scan of 120 queues at 30 s steps found only this one, refined to the second). New sky unit test target_in_coordinates_of_grid_date (grid in 2060) fails on the old code and passes with the fix. Driver version 0x03000026 -> 0x03000027 (same line as ticket ffac50e4, identical change). flow check whitespace+unit passed. Integration test_agent_scheduler: 1st run 172/173 (failed case not captured), then 173/173 twice; investigating whether it is a flake.

Integration test_agent_scheduler on the final tree: 4 runs, 3 x 173/173 and the first 172/173; the failing case of the first run was not captured and did not recur in three logged runs. Treated as an intermittent timing failure, not attributed to this change; not investigated further.
Building and running scheduler sky/plan unit tests in the worktree

Correction (confirmed by review and by the implementer's own run after the epoch fix): wall-clock epoch drift did NOT cause the failure. The old fixture (39th queue, now + 3009) fails with and without the epoch fix and at every wall-clock time tried (gap about 81 against about 1e-3 per day of drift); the fixture was stale against the plan code, and re-deriving it (67th queue, now + 13183) repaired the test, which also passes with the old sky.c. Why tree 0bb29906 passed the unit check at 01:43 UTC stays unexplained (a stale incremental build is possible). The epoch change is a separate valid fix: plans for fixed inputs no longer depend on when they are computed (verified by the reviewer with a time() shim for 2023, 2026 and 2060). Version: ticket ffac50e4 makes the identical 0x03000027 change; whichever ticket closes second must go to 0x03000028.
